text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client who has severe anemia and requires a transfusion of packed red blood cells (PRBCs). Which of the following four actions should the nurse plan to take?
A. Check vital signs before transfusion.
C. Prime the blood tubing with 0.9% sodium chloride.
D. Transfuse the PRBCs within 6 hours.
E. Check the expiration date of the PRBCs with a second nurse.

Correct answers: A. Check vital signs before transfusion.; B. Insert an 18-gauge intravenous (IV) line.; C. Prime the blood tubing with 0.9% sodium chloride.; E. Check the expiration date of the PRBCs with a second nurse.
notes: Correct: Take baseline vital signs, use a large-bore (18-gauge) IV, prime the tubing with 0.9% sodium chloride only, and verify the blood product and expiration with a second licensed nurse.
Not correct: A unit of PRBCs should be completed within 4 hours of leaving the blood bank; 6 hours is too long.
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)
